changes: King: confidence lowered from high to medium. The name is corrupt, and Jagajjyotirmalla of Bhaktapur is usually dated to c. 1613/14–1637, after NS 730 (1609/10). Added a note on the conflict.
ce_approx given as 1609–1610. Pauṣa of NS 730 falls in Dec 1609 or Jan 1610.
Notes expanded with the reign/date problem and the standard scribal formula.

notes: The king's name 'jaggatrayeti malla deva' is corrupt. The most likely reading is Jagajjyotirmalla of Bhaktapur, but his reign is usually dated c. 1613/14–1637, a few years after NS 730 (1609/10), when Trailokyamalla was still ruling Bhaktapur. Jagattraya ('three worlds') means the same as trailokya, so a garbled 'Trailokyamalla' cannot be ruled out. Either the date is misread, the colophon names Jagajjyotirmalla while he was a co-ruler or crown prince, or the name stands for another king. 'jatra(!)ditvā(!) tatra rīkhita(!) mama ṣo(!)na diyate(!)' is the standard scribal formula 'yādṛśaṃ pustakaṃ dṛṣṭvā tādṛśaṃ likhitaṃ mayā / mama doṣo na dīyate'. 'riṅgaṃ(!)purāṇe' stands for Liṅgapurāṇe. 'siṃha' is kept as part of the scribe's name.
